method: Independent recomputation in Python (stdlib) from the 15 committed records.jsonl.gz, by validator/recompute.py, written without reading analysis/*.mjs, summary.json or the producer's interval code (results.md, README.md and PROTOCOL.md were read before; results.json was opened only after own-numbers.json was first written; afterwards, seeing that compare pairs (session, target) means, the validator added a target-level linearised t as the protocol reading and a null control; no ratio, pricing or pairing code changed). Pricing re-implemented from the documented band formula priced_gae(w) = G - C + w (U + n_C) (AGENTS.md 5a; band.rs) with the pinned char2 calibration rows; every recovered log re-checked by own GF(2^n) arithmetic; strictest incumbent chosen on the same data (pooled and per replicate); intervals by linearised t and stratified bootstraps (4000 resamples, seed 20261002). Replay: ecbench rebuilt by the validator from the recorded source, verify --replay-all on all 15 sessions (nonce-designated sample B27-r1, B21-r2, B21-r3), and two fresh sessions (n24, n27; 24 new targets, 1 round, nonce-derived seeds) with rho-neg, the strictest incumbents plus one size beyond the bracket, ksum4 and ksum5 at the frozen sizes. No commit was made.

dispatch_change_review.commit: d87eb39548 (one match arm in solve_ic_binary, src/cryptanalysis/ecbench/methods.rs: "ksum" => KSumOracle::new(ms))
dispatch_change_review.generic_over_group: KSumOracle implements DecompositionOracle<G> for every G: CountedGroup (ic_framework/plugins.rs); KSumTable (ic_boundary.rs) uses only CountedGroup::add/neg/key/is_identity
dispatch_change_review.every_group_op_charged: BinaryGroup::add increments ops.adds, ::double ops.doubles (ic_boundary.rs, impl CountedGroup for BinaryGroup); the table build adds go to build_ops and are merged into the oracle_setup phase; each probe's k-1 confirming adds go to the relation ops; probes are counted as lookups (calibrated at w = 0, repriced at w by the band), inserts as table_insert_attempts behind counted:table_insert_attempts (priced at w)
dispatch_change_review.build_cost_measured_equals_combinatorial: oracle_setup adds = sum_{d=2..k} C(A,d) 2^(d-1) and insert attempts = C(A,k) 2^(k-1) on every one of the 4320 measured ksum4/ksum5 records (A = abscissae; e.g. n27 ksum5 A = 12: 17644 adds, 12672 inserts); 0 mismatches
dispatch_change_review.negation_fold_valid_in_char2: table key is key(P) >> 1 with FastPoint::pack = 2(x+1) + [y > x XOR y]; -P = (x, x XOR y) (FastCurve::neg), so the sign bit flips and key >> 1 = x + 1 is shared by +-P exactly; a probe hit is confirmed by recomputing the k-sum and comparing with target or neg(target), and the base's neg_index is built from the same neg (FactorBase::from_column_map with neg_key_of = inst.fast.neg(p).pack())
dispatch_change_review.soundness: a key match that is neither +target nor -target is rejected (no relation), so a wrong key could only lose completeness, never produce a false relation
dispatch_change_review.verification_independent_of_oracle: the runner checks [k]G == target in its own (parent) process with inst.mul_generator_exact (runner.rs, audit_verification), separate from the solving child; the validator additionally re-checked every recovered log with its own Python GF(2^n) arithmetic (certificates below)

build.explanation: The two ELF files differ only in symbol-table text and the linker build-id: (1) 352 local symbols carry an LLVM promoted-local suffix `.llvm.15188867642286278132` in the recorded binary and `.llvm.8458451346301811158` in the validator's (a module hash that depends on the build directory; the validator used a separate CARGO_TARGET_DIR), which also explains the 352-byte size difference (95489904 vs 95489552 bytes; one digit shorter per occurrence); no other string differs; (2) after `strip`, both files are 86539696 bytes and differ in exactly 20 bytes at offsets 0x32c-0x33f, the GNU build-id descriptor of .note.gnu.build-id (a hash over the unstripped output). The loaded sections .text, .rodata, .data and .data.rel.ro are byte-identical. The validator build is therefore the same program; its replays reproduced every recorded count.

certificates.method: own affine GF(2^n) double-and-add in Python: [recovered]G == target, target on curve, 0 <= recovered < r; generator on curve, [r]G = O, r prime

pricing_audit.formula: priced_gae(w) = G - C + w (U + n_C); S = priced_gae / sqrt(r); C, n_C = calibrated native (lookups, target_guard_probes, row_ops, ...) priced by docs/ic/calibration.json char2 row of each curve; U = cost.unpriced counts (rho: canonicalisations_uncharged) + table_insert_attempts where the counted: marker is present
pricing_audit.checks: every IC record: G == sum(adds + doubles) + C and G - C integral; every rho record: G == sum of phase gae; every record: recorded s == G / sqrt(r); no nonzero native counter in PRICED_NATIVE left unpriced by a missing pinned unit; no unpriced counter without a count
pricing_audit.matches_producer_band_files: mean S per arm and weight equal band/B*.json mean_s to ~1e-15 (checked after own numbers were written)

intervals.protocol_reading: upper = max(linearised-t on (session, target) means over rounds, target-cluster bootstrap stratified by session); percentile, type-7 quantiles, Python random.Random
intervals.pair_level_reading: max(linearised-t on (session, target, round) pairs, pair bootstrap stratified by session)
intervals.note: the producer's ecbench compare upper ends (max per row and candidate) are 0.4-1.4% wider than the validator's protocol reading; every L1 decision is identical under both readings

checks.rho_reference: rho-neg (rho.negation) runs in every session on the same curve, targets and algorithm seeds as every IC arm, in the same binary; random-binary curves (not Koblitz) have A = 2 (automorphisms_available 2 in every record), so negation is the strongest symmetry available; rho-neg is cheaper than ksum5 at every weight on every row (order holds across the band)

null_controls.reading: two incumbents that differ only in base size give ratios 1.000-1.11 with intervals of about +-1.5%; where they are tied (n24 w=0: inc-n80/inc-n67 1.0014 [0.987, 1.016]; n27 w=1: inc-n150/inc-n178 1.0001 [0.989, 1.011]) the interval covers 1, so the interval machinery does not manufacture the 32-54% effects
null_controls.aa_arm: rho-neg-aa shares rho-neg's seeds, so the A/A arm is identical by construction (0 differing pairs) and carries no noise information; the protocol's noise control is the replicate spread delta (max/min of per-session mean S at w = 0 over inc-tb, rho-neg, ksum5, ksum4)
null_controls.trend: the ksum5 ratio falls monotonically with field size (1.14, 1.04, 0.68, 0.64, 0.46 for n15..n27 at w = 0), as a k-sum table against a pair table is expected to (heuristic r^(5/9) vs r^(2/3) balanced cost, ratio ~ r^(-1/9): 0.68 at n21 predicts ~0.48 at n27; observed 0.46); this is a consistency check, not a claim

heuristic_and_cost_model.unit: ecbench.gae (counted group additions and doublings; S = GAE/sqrt(r)); unpriced native work priced at w in {0, 0.1, 1} GAE per operation (AGENTS.md 5a)
heuristic_and_cost_model.optimistic_assumptions: one affine group operation = 1 GAE for every arm (field inversions not separately priced); IC walk bookkeeping counters (walk_mix_hashes, walk_modr_adds, under counted:walk_bookkeeping) and rho's cycle_window_word_ops are outside the band's U for all arms; pricing the IC walk counters would charge the incumbents more than the candidates (about 4x more trials per run on n27), so leaving them out does not favour the candidate; the IC-vs-rho gap is computed under the band's definition of U and would move if these counters were priced
heuristic_and_cost_model.memory: max RSS per run about 17-18 MB for every IC arm on n27 (ksum5 median 17200 KiB, inc-n150 17576 KiB, rho-neg 14896 KiB); ksum5 table 12672 entries vs inc-n150 22500 on n27; memory is not binding and not part of the claim
heuristic_and_cost_model.success_probability: every one of the 25920 study records (19440 measured, 6480 warm-up) and 288 fresh records completed and verified (no censoring, no timeouts); expected cost is the mean over runs, nothing extrapolated
heuristic_and_cost_model.scale: n = 15..27 (log2 r 14.0-24.4) only; no transfer to larger fields is claimed (PROTOCOL.md 'Not claimed'); the claimed improvement is measured on the exact rows, so inventor-protocol section 6 extrapolation steps do not arise
heuristic_and_cost_model.incumbent_tuning: tuned incumbents bracket the pilot optimum: n21 interior (62 of 43/62/87) at every w; n27 interior at w = 0, 0.1 (150) and at the upper edge at w = 1 (178 by 0.003 S over 150); n24 interior at w = 0 (67), upper edge (80) at w = 0.1, 1. Fresh validator sessions added one size beyond each edge: n27 inc-n210 is worse than inc-n150 at every w; n24 inc-n94 is 1.5% cheaper than inc-n80 at w = 1 (25.55 vs 25.94, 24 targets), which would move the n24 w = 1 ratio from about 0.605 to about 0.62; immaterial to L1
